item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/8/2026.

IMPORTANT: This is a senior role requiring 7+ years of experience in healthcare policy analysis. A master's degree is strongly preferred. It is not suitable for early-career candidates.

The American Medical Association (AMA) is the nation's largest professional association of physicians, dedicated to promoting the art and science of medicine and the betterment of public health. The Lead Policy Analyst on the Digital Health & AI team will develop and shape AMA policy positions on digital health and AI policy, recommend new policies, and assist in the development of corresponding AMA strategies and initiatives. This is a hybrid position requiring 3 days/week in the Washington, DC office (25 Massachusetts Avenue NW). Some travel required. Salary $109,866-$145,344 plus incentive plan.

Key responsibilities include (AMA Policy Development and Research): developing policy reports, reviews, position statements, comment letters, written testimonies, and presentation materials to influence the policy landscape; analyzing and preparing correspondence and briefing materials for Senior Management on key digital health and AI issues; monitoring state and federal legislative and regulatory digital health and AI developments and developing guidance for physicians on the implications of these developments; and creating and contributing to new and updated educational and communications resources and events. (Internal and External Relationships): collaborating with internal business units including Advocacy, Enterprise Communications, and Center for Optimal Health Outcomes to ensure consistent messaging; contributing to the planning and implementing of convenings, briefings, conferences, and presentations related to digital health policies; building and maintaining external relationships including medical specialty societies, industry stakeholders, and coalitions; representing the AMA at external meetings; and assisting in the management of AMA coalitions.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree required, master's degree strongly preferred; 7+ years of experience in healthcare policy analysis in an academic, government, corporate, or nonprofit setting; knowledge of digital health and AI trends in the healthcare industry required; knowledge of data privacy and HIPAA highly preferred; demonstrated ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders and synthesize multiple viewpoints into actionable recommendations; proven ability to conduct in-depth policy research and analysis and translate complex issues into clear, concise written materials for a variety of audiences; strong project management and communication skills; and polished speaking and presentation skills.

Compensation and logistics: salary $109,866-$145,344 plus incentive plan. Comprehensive AMA benefits. Hybrid in Washington, DC (3 days/week in office). Some travel required.

item.description:

The Urban Institute is a research-to-impact institution dedicated to improving lives and strengthening communities through evidence-based practices and policies. The Justice Policy Center (JPC) conducts objective, interdisciplinary research and policy analysis across issues including community safety, policing, courts, corrections, reentry, violence prevention, victimization, youth justice, and system reform. The Research Assistant will support research, evaluation, and technical assistance projects focused on promoting safe communities and an equitable and effective criminal legal system. Individuals with lived experience related to the criminal legal system and applicants from communities disproportionately affected by criminal justice involvement are strongly encouraged to apply. Key responsibilities include: conducting literature reviews and background research on the criminal legal system, public safety, and justice and safety-related topics; collecting, cleaning, managing, and analyzing quantitative and/or qualitative data; supporting data collection activities including surveys, interviews, focus groups, site visits, and administrative data projects; assisting with statistical analyses using software such as Stata, R, Python, SAS, or other analytical tools; drafting sections of reports, research briefs, memos, presentations, blog posts, and other dissemination products; developing tables, figures, data visualizations, and descriptive summaries of findings; participating in project meetings and supporting project coordination, scheduling, note-taking, and tracking deliverables; contributing to proposal development; and supporting the translation of research findings for policymakers, practitioners, community stakeholders, and public audiences.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree or associate's degree with equivalent experience (preferably in public policy, criminology, sociology, economics, statistics, political science, psychology, public health, data science, or a related field); demonstrated interest in one or more topics in justice and public safety policy; strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills including prior experience conducting quantitative and/or qualitative research; excellent written and verbal communication skills; and strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
